notes:
- Back leaves the character page, not the page behind it: A back press with a character's page open closed the sheet *and* the title page under it, so one press dropped the reader on Home with the title they were reading gone. The press was never the sheet's: the bottom sheet's own dismissal is not reached from that window, so it fell through to the screen's back handler and popped the destination the title page was drawn over. The sheet answers back itself now, which is how the appearance editor and My Entry already unwind - one layer per press, so the next press leaves the title.
- The poster flies out of the poster you pressed: Opening a title from a character's page or from a studio's credits flew its cover in from the wrong place - sometimes from the bottom of the display, sometimes from the top - because the rectangle recorded at the press was measured from the window the card was in and then spent as if it were screen space. A bottom sheet is anchored to the bottom edge, so for every poster inside one the error was most of a screen. The two windows share one frame of reference now: the card records in screen pixels and the page moves that into its own window once the display has placed it, so the copy grows out of the artwork under the finger whichever surface opened it.
- The trailer shows its picture: The audio worked and the picture did not: the official trailer played - sound, the player's chrome, the title - over a black rectangle, because a video surface inside a floating dialog window was left to the platform's default compositing, which drops the video plane while the rest of the page draws normally. The player asks for a hardware layer now, so its whole output, video included, arrives as one texture. A trailer whose id is not one YouTube could have issued no longer opens a dead player either - that tap goes to the browser, which is where the card's own escape hatch leads.
- The stats strip counts each status once: The profile's Status Distribution grouped its segments by the raw token AniList sent, and `ListStatuses` aliases the spellings API v1 used - `WATCHING`, `FINISHED`, `ON_HOLD`, `CLEARED`. An entry cached under one of those became its own segment: the strip read 'Watching' twice with the account's count split between the two, the alias sorted to the end because the fixed order knows only the six current tokens, and the segments stopped adding up to the total printed under them. The tokens are normalized before they are grouped (and their amounts summed, so neither half is lost), which is the one list the editor, the Library chips and this card all read.
- Labels no longer depend on the phone's language: Three comparisons lower-cased or upper-cased a token off the wire with no locale, which is the device's: on a Turkish phone `PLANNING` lower-cased to 'plannıng' with a dotless i, so every activity row in the feed printed its raw enum - 'CURRENT', 'COMPLETED' - instead of 'Watched' or 'Plans to watch'; `Overlord IV` upper-cased to 'İV' and stopped being a roman numeral, which silently handed that season the shared series poster; and a person's `type` was upper-cased before it was compared with `MANGA`. All three compare case-insensitively now, and the feed, the season layer and the profile read the same token the API wrote.
- A trailer card keeps its own poster: The trailer card's thumbnail was memoized on the validated video id rather than on the id it had just read, so a trailer whose id YouTube could not have issued - the ones that now open in the browser instead of a dead player - asked YouTube for `vi/null/hqdefault.jpg` and drew a broken card.
